data.name: Lucilia
data.gender_notes: Lucilia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin 'lux' meaning 'light'. The name Lucilia was given to those who brought light or hope in times of darkness. The name Lucilia carries the meaning “Light, Bringer of Light” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Lucilia usually hope their child will grow to embody light, bringer of light and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Lucilia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Light, Bringer of Light.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lucilia total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: Lucilia, derived from the Latin 'lux' meaning 'light', was a name given to those who brought illumination and hope to their communities. In ancient Rome, Lucilia was regarded as a goddess of light, fertility, and funerals. The name became popular among early Christians for those who lived a virtuous and inspiring life, spreading light and hope to those around them.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Lucilia holds deep spiritual significance as a reminder of the power of light and hope. It serves as a symbol of the transformative power of the human spirit, offering comfort, guidance, and faith in difficult times. Additionally, it represents the celestial connection we all share, urging us to live our lives in a way that brings light and joy to those around us and to the world.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Lucilia: Bringer of Light and Grace. Derived from the Latin word for light, "lux," and the Italian word for sweetness, "dolce," symbolizing the illumination and sweetness of God's love.

historical_references.reference: In early Christian hagiography, a virgin martyr named Lucilia is mentioned. She was said to have been martyred during the reign of Emperor Diocletian (284-305 AD) in the city of Cremona in present-day Italy. Her feast day is celebrated on August 2nd.

In medieval Europe, Lucilia was also known as a healer saint. The legend tells that she was a noblewoman who lived in Constantinople during the reign of Emperor Theodosius I (375-395 AD). She is said to have possessed the power to heal wounds by applying a balm made from herbs. Her feast day is celebrated on February 22nd.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Lucilia is increasingly being used as a unique and stylish moniker for social media influencers, particularly those with a focus on fashion and aesthetics. Lucilia can be found on various platforms such as Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. On Instagram, she might showcase her impeccable sense of style and curated feed. On TikTok, she could create engaging and trendy content to amass a large followership. On YouTube, Lucilia may run a fashion-focused channel, featuring makeup tutorials, fashion hauls, and outfit inspiration. Generally, the usage of the name Lucilia on these platforms represents a blend of beauty, creativity, and individuality.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Mary Lucilia in Athens, Greece credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Lucilia, which means "Light, Bringer of Light". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
